newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures revive spread buying.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures revive spread buying.

text.p: Prices for U.S. energy futures revived in light Monday ACCESS trade, after a sharp sell-off during the floor session, traders said.
The floor session saw crudes drop below $26, triggering automated sell orders which pulled the contract down 90 cents to $25.19 a barrel.
"The market was a little bit overbought," a trader said, noting that forecasts of warmer temperatures in the high-consumption U.S. Northeast lessened supply fears.
But the region's current cold weather and spread buyig pushed prices back up overnight. February crude traded $25.25 at 1727 PST, up six cents a barrel with 600 lots traded.
NYMEX February heating oil firmed slightly to 69.95 cents a barrel, up 0.25 cent gallon from 69.70 cents amid volume of 100 lots.
Gasoline futures were barely changed at 68.10 cents a gallon, up 0.01 cents from the settle. About 160 lots traded in February out of 150 overall.
